reason: The hypothesis relies on premises about mechanical benefits of coherent nanoprecipitates (supported by E1) and general phase stability of HEAs (partly supported by E2/E3), but the critical premise that coherent nanoprecipitates enhance thermal conductivity is not supported by any cited evidence, and the specific annealing conditions are not validated by the cited studies.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates in W-based HEAs can simultaneously enhance strength and ductility by facilitating dislocation transmission and relieving stress concentrations.
Controlled low-temperature annealing can induce coherent nanoprecipitate formation in a W-based HEA without deleterious phase coarsening.
Coherent nanoprecipitates reduce interfacial thermal resistance and improve heat carrier (phonon/electron) transmission, thereby enhancing thermal conductivity.
The multicomponent mixing in W-based HEAs provides sufficient phase stability to support coherent nanoprecipitate formation during annealing.
The proposed annealing treatment will not compromise structural integrity under intermediate reactor conditions (300–800 °C).
